children: is preparing for a leadership change as Tim Cook concludes his 15-year tenure as chief executive and John Ternus takes over the role on Sept. 1, according to a company memo.

Cook used his final message to employees to reflect on his time at the company and thank staff for their contribution. During his tenure, Apple's revenue grew to more than $416 billion, while its market value increased from roughly $350 billion to about $4.6 trillion.
In his note, Cook said working with Apple employees brought out the best in him and described the company's culture as an important part of its progress. He also expressed confidence in John Ternus.

Ternus, a 25-year Apple veteran, will become CEO after leading hardware engineering since 2021 as senior vice president. His responsibilities have included major product development across the iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods and Apple Watch, as well as Apple's move toward its own processors.
The transition comes shortly before Apple's Sept. 9 product event, where the company is expected to introduce its latest iPhone lineup and potentially a foldable model.
The leadership handoff puts Ternus' product strategy under scrutiny as Apple enters a key product cycle.

title: CEO Tim Cook Sends Goodbye Message to Apple Staff as 15-Year Run Ends
